messages.body_plain:
These two lines should be inside the server function:

data_planes <- data.frame()
makeReactiveBinding("data_planes")

See https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/scoping.html for an explanation why.

Also your i variable shouldn't be declared at the top level, it should probably be inside the server function? I don't at all understand what its purpose is, or the logic of your plotting code.

It looks to me like the expression returned from your renderRglwidget code block should be rglwidget(). See https://github.com/wave-electron/Shiny-RGLwidget-Example- as a random example I found on github (I haven't tried running it).

Declaring an output inside of observeEvent isn't correct; you'll find that as soon as you click the Update button once, the plot updates as soon as the data changes (i.e. not waiting for Update to be clicked again). I go into the reasons why this is in the beginning of the first video here: https://www.rstudio.com/resources/videos/effective-reactive-programming/ What you want to do is something more like:

output$plot <- renderRglwidget({
  # Take a dependency on the plotbutton
  input$plotbutton

  isolate({
    # All of the rest of your logic goes here...
    if (i <= nrow(data_planes)) {
      # etc, etc
    }
    rglwidget()
  })
})

messages.body_plain:
The conditions in your conditionalPanel, e.g. `input.inputId=='Normal'`, aren't correct; there isn't any input called "inputId". Instead, you need to replace that string with the actual variable name. Here's one example:

        conditionalPanel(condition = sprintf("input.%s=='Normal'", paste0("moreControls", input$invar[i])),

          textInput("invarpdfmean","Please Select Input Variable Mean:",0.25),
          textInput("invarpdfsd","Please Select Input Variable Standard Deviation", 0.02)),

But I have also highlighted two id's that will also need to be made dynamic; as written, there could be multiple textInputs with "invarpdfmean" as an input on the same page, which isn't allowed.

It might be a bit of a stretch for you right now but you may eventually want to use a Shiny module for the per-input controls:
https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/modules.html Shiny modules have a bit of a learning curve themselves, but the resulting code will be cleaner and easier to reason about.

Hi all,

I have a (small) package where I re-implement some of the basic inputs of shiny in such a way that the labels appear on the left and the input on the right. For this, I "hack" into shiny using ::: to have access to functions like choicesWithNames, firstChoice, selectizeIt and so forth. Obviously this prevents my own package from being cran-worthy. Hence I have 3 possible approaches:

- copy all these functions literally into my package (I can't import non-exported objects)
- fork Shiny, export the functions I need, add some help pages for them and hope my fork gets pulled into shiny.
- fork Shiny, add my selectInline, textInline, numericInline etc functions, and hope my fork gets pulled into shiny.
- fork Shiny, add an "inline" option to all the standard input functions, and hope my fork gets pulled into shiny.

My questions:

1. Which method would you pick?

2. I'd love it when I can just add what I need to shiny, but I haven't been able to find somebody who could tell me which option fits best into the underlying design choices made by the shiny dev team.

Cheers
Joris

> Thanks for your bug report. Tried to understand the problem for some hours, and now that I found, I can't think of a way to fix it :
> Drawn features are exported to R in GeoJSON format. GeoJSON doesn't handle the circle geometry, and circles are then stored as points with a radius attribute (outside the geometry).

I think I found your issue though. It's a simple typo.

In the UI, you call the module and give it an id "ImpactQList1":

ImpactQuestInput("ImpactQList1")

However, when you call the server module, you use a different id: "ImpactQlist1" (notice that lowercase l, when it should have been an uppercase L)

callModule(ImpactQuest,"ImpactQlist1",questionSet)

So, you see, in this case, there was no problem with the code logic and the issue was a simple typo. The problem asking for help without a runnable example is precisely this. I ended up spending a lot more time making the code runnable than the time I took to find the bug. So you have an idea of what a MRE would look like for this situation, here's what I got:

# ------------------------------------ MODULE ----------------------------------
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# module UI
modUI <- function(id) {
  ns <- NS(id)

  tagList(
    h4(textOutput(ns("labelQc01"))),
    radioButtons(ns("c1"), "Please Select:", choices = c("")),
    tags$hr(style = "border-color: darkblue;"),

    h4(textOutput(ns("labelQc02"))),
    radioButtons(ns("c2"), "Please Select:", choices = c("")),
    tags$hr(style = "border-color: darkblue;"),

    h4(textOutput(ns("labelQc03"))),
    radioButtons(ns("c3"), "Please Select:", choices = c("")),
    tags$hr(style = "border-color: darkblue;"),

    h4(textOutput(ns("labelQc04"))),
    radioButtons(ns("c4"), "Please Select:", choices = c(""))
  )
}

# module server
mod <- function(input, output, session, questionSet) {

  createLabel <- function(name) {
    paste0(name, ": ",
      questionSet[questionSet$QID == name,]$Element.Question,
      sep = "")
  }

  output$labelQc01 <- renderText({ createLabel("C01") })
  output$labelQc02 <- renderText({ createLabel("C02") })
  output$labelQc03 <- renderText({ createLabel("C03") })
  output$labelQc04 <- renderText({ createLabel("C04") })

  createOptions <- function(row) {
    as.character(questionSet[row,5:ncol(questionSet)])
  }

  updateRadioButtons(session, "c1", choices = createOptions(1))
  updateRadioButtons(session, "c2", choices = createOptions(2))
  updateRadioButtons(session, "c3", choices = createOptions(3))
  updateRadioButtons(session, "c4", choices = createOptions(4))
}

# ----------------------------------- MAIN APP ---------------------------------
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

library(shiny)

questionSet <- tibble::tibble(
  QID = c("C01", "C02", "C03", "C04"),
  Element.Question = c(
    "Do you like icecream?",
    "Do you like sunny days?",
    "Do you like going to the movies?",
    "Do you like coffee?"
  ),
  col3 = c(character(1), character(1), character(1), character(1)),
  col4 = c(character(1), character(1), character(1), character(1)),
  Option1 = c("Yes", "Yes", "Yes", "Yes"),
  Option2 = c("No", "No", "No", "No"),
  Option3 = c("Maybe", "Maybe", "Maybe", "Maybe")
)

ui <- navbarPage("Select:",
  tabPanel("Inputs", modUI("questions"))
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  callModule(mod, "questions", questionSet = questionSet)
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

I cannot seem to access the results of a radiobutton that is dynamically generated in a Shiny Module UI.  In the simple example included (thanks to Barbara Borges) I try to simply print the choice made when selecting a radiobutton for input question 1 and display that choice in the output tab.  The app seems to believe that the input (input$id) is null:

# ------------------------------------ MODULE ----------------------------------
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# module UI
modUI <- function(id) {
  ns <- NS(id)

  tagList(
    h4(textOutput(ns("labelQc01"))),
    radioButtons(ns("c1"), "Please Select:", choices = c("")),
    tags$hr(style = "border-color: darkblue;"),

    h4(textOutput(ns("labelQc02"))),
    radioButtons(ns("c2"), "Please Select:", choices = c("")),
    tags$hr(style = "border-color: darkblue;"),

    h4(textOutput(ns("labelQc03"))),
    radioButtons(ns("c3"), "Please Select:", choices = c("")),
    tags$hr(style = "border-color: darkblue;"),

    h4(textOutput(ns("labelQc04"))),
    radioButtons(ns("c4"), "Please Select:", choices = c(""))
  )
}

# module server
mod <- function(input, output, session, questionSet) {

  createLabel <- function(name) {
    paste0(name, ": ",
           questionSet[questionSet$QID == name,]$Element.Question,
           sep = "")
  }

  output$labelQc01 <- renderText({ createLabel("C01") })
  output$labelQc02 <- renderText({ createLabel("C02") })
  output$labelQc03 <- renderText({ createLabel("C03") })
  output$labelQc04 <- renderText({ createLabel("C04") })

  createOptions <- function(row) {
    as.character(questionSet[row,5:ncol(questionSet)])
  }

  updateRadioButtons(session, "c1", choices = createOptions(1))
  updateRadioButtons(session, "c2", choices = createOptions(2))
  updateRadioButtons(session, "c3", choices = createOptions(3))
  updateRadioButtons(session, "c4", choices = createOptions(4))
}

# ----------------------------------- MAIN APP ---------------------------------
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

library(shiny)

questionSet <- tibble::tibble(
  QID = c("C01", "C02", "C03", "C04"),
  Element.Question = c(
    "Do you like icecream?",
    "Do you like sunny days?",
    "Do you like going to the movies?",
    "Do you like coffee?"
  ),
  col3 = c(character(1), character(1), character(1), character(1)),
  col4 = c(character(1), character(1), character(1), character(1)),
  Option1 = c("Yes", "Yes", "Yes", "Yes"),
  Option2 = c("No", "No", "No", "No"),
  Option3 = c("Maybe", "Maybe", "Maybe", "Maybe")
)

ui <- navbarPage("Select:",
                 tabPanel("Inputs", modUI("questions")),
                 tabPanel("Outputs",
                          textOutput("testthis"),
                          textOutput("testthat"),
                          verbatimTextOutput("debug")
)
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  callModule(mod, "questions", questionSet = questionSet)
  output$testthis <- renderText({1:17})
  output$testthat <- renderText(ifelse(is.null(input$ns("c3")),"This IS NULL",input$ns("c3")))
#  print(output$testthis))

output$debug <- renderPrint({
  input$c1
})

}

shinyApp(ui, server)

messages.subject: Re: Usuing UI elements created inside a Shiny Module
messages.subject_clean: Usuing UI elements created inside a Shiny Module
messages.body_plain:
This is by design. From the modules article: <https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/modules.html>

>  The input, output, and session objects we’re provided with are special, in that they are scoped to the specific namespace that matches up with our UI function.
>
>
>
> On the flip side, the input, output, and session cannot be used to access inputs/outputs that are outside of the namespace, nor can they directly access reactive expressions and reactive values from elsewhere in the application (OK, technically, lexically scoped reactive expressions/values can be used, but that’s it ).
>
>
>
> These restrictions are by design, and they are important. The goal is not to prevent modules from interacting with their containing apps, but rather, to make these interactions explicit. If a module needs to use a reactive expression, take the reactive expression as a function parameter. If a module wants to return reactive expressions to the calling app, then return a list of reactive expressions from the function.

As the last sentence makes clear, you need to return the values that you may want to use on the main app (though you should strive to keep the code encapsulated in the module itself as much as possible). Here's what it would look like in your example (taking away the unnecessary outputs and tabPanels for ease of visualization):

# ------------------------------------ MODULE ----------------------------------
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# module UI
modUI <- function(id) {
  ns <- NS(id)

  tagList(
    h4(textOutput(ns("labelQc01"))),
    radioButtons(ns("c1"), "Please Select:", choices = c("")),
    tags$hr(style = "border-color: darkblue;"),

    h4(textOutput(ns("labelQc02"))),
    radioButtons(ns("c2"), "Please Select:", choices = c("")),
    tags$hr(style = "border-color: darkblue;"),

    h4(textOutput(ns("labelQc03"))),
    radioButtons(ns("c3"), "Please Select:", choices = c("")),
    tags$hr(style = "border-color: darkblue;"),

    h4(textOutput(ns("labelQc04"))),
    radioButtons(ns("c4"), "Please Select:", choices = c(""))
  )
}

# module server
mod <- function(input, output, session, questionSet) {

  createLabel <- function(name) {
    paste0(name, ": ",
      questionSet[questionSet$QID == name,]$Element.Question,
      sep = "")
  }

  output$labelQc01 <- renderText({ createLabel("C01") })
  output$labelQc02 <- renderText({ createLabel("C02") })
  output$labelQc03 <- renderText({ createLabel("C03") })
  output$labelQc04 <- renderText({ createLabel("C04") })

  createOptions <- function(row) {
    as.character(questionSet[row,5:ncol(questionSet)])
  }

  updateRadioButtons(session, "c1", choices = createOptions(1))
  updateRadioButtons(session, "c2", choices = createOptions(2))
  updateRadioButtons(session, "c3", choices = createOptions(3))
  updateRadioButtons(session, "c4", choices = createOptions(4))

  return(list(
    c1 = reactive(input$c1),
    c2 = reactive(input$c2),
    c3 = reactive(input$c3),
    c4 = reactive(input$c4)

  ))
}

# ----------------------------------- MAIN APP ---------------------------------
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

library(shiny)

questionSet <- tibble::tibble(
  QID = c("C01", "C02", "C03", "C04"),
  Element.Question = c(
    "Do you like icecream?",
    "Do you like sunny days?",
    "Do you like going to the movies?",
    "Do you like coffee?"
  ),
  col3 = c(character(1), character(1), character(1), character(1)),
  col4 = c(character(1), character(1), character(1), character(1)),
  Option1 = c("Yes", "Yes", "Yes", "Yes"),
  Option2 = c("No", "No", "No", "No"),
  Option3 = c("Maybe", "Maybe", "Maybe", "Maybe")
)

ui <- fluidPage(
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(uiOutput("answers")),
    mainPanel(modUI("questions"))

  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  results <- callModule(mod, "questions", questionSet = questionSet)

  output$answers <- renderUI({
    tagList(
      h4("Answers from module, displayed from main app"),
      div(strong("c1"), " answer: ", results$c1()),
      div(strong("c2"), " answer: ", results$c2()),
      div(strong("c3"), " answer: ", results$c3()),
      div(strong("c4"), " answer: ", results$c4())
    )
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

messages.body_plain:
If you're using a Mac that has a Retina display, then it seems likely that the problem you're having is related to image size. When Shiny renders a plot for a client that has a Retina display, it will double the resolution of the output file.

If you use png() to try to create a very large image, it will give an error. (Note that type="cairo" is the default on Linux, but not on Mac.)

> png(width=1000,height=40000, type = "cairo")
Error in png(width = 1000, height = 40000, type = "cairo") :
  unable to start device 'png'
In addition: Warning message:
In png(width = 1000, height = 40000, type = "cairo") :
  cairo error 'invalid value (typically too big) for the size of the input (surface, pattern, etc.)'

One possible way around this is to use the renderImage() function. Unlike renderPlot(), it will not automatically double the resolution of the output image. See ?renderImage for some examples.

-Winston

CentOS is an OS designed to be "safe" and secure and stable for a long time. They are slower to update packages and have longer release cycles. Ubuntu released more quickly, has LTS versions every couple of years, and keeps packages more on the bleeding edge.

This means, for example, that without any tinkering you're going to get a newer default version of R out of the box on ubuntu than CentOS.

Use CentOS if

1. You like and are comfortable with it.
2.  You're working with a team of people who are familiar with the Red Hat ecosystem, and therefore they are more comfortable with CentOS
3.  You have some other apps that require CentOS

Otherwise, I'd just go with Ubuntu.  I think you'll find things will be easier as its more popular and had a wider user base and updates more frequently.

Erik

messages.subject_clean: No validate() message displayed for ‘non-flickering’ DT
messages.body_plain:
I had relied on sliderInputs to ensure that only valid entries be displayed in a DT coded to eliminate re-rendering of the entire table whenever an input changes. (see the final comment (by yihui) at https://github.com/rstudio/DT/issues/168)

After swapping some sliderInputs for numericInputs (to satisfy a user), I added validation code for the new numericInputs.

This worked fine — i.e., the validation message was displayed as needed — when the output was either a ggplot or (I found by playing around) a ’flickering’ DT — one for which the data was un-wrapped from isolate() in the server function call to DT::renderDataTable().

The behaviors of flickering and non-flickering DTs are illustrated in the following code.

library(shiny)
library(DT)

shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    titlePanel('Inputs'),
    sidebarLayout(
      sidebarPanel(

        numericInput('numeric_input', 'This entry must be > 300!', value = 500),

        sliderInput('slider_input', 'Some other input', min = 0, max = 1, value = 0.5, step = 0.1)
      ),

      mainPanel(

        h4('The Non-flickering DT', align = 'center'),
        tags$li('GOOD: doesn\'t re-render entire table when change valid entry'),
        tags$li('BAD: does not display validation message when numeric input <= 300'),
        br(),
        DT::dataTableOutput('non_flickering_dt'),

        hr(),

        h4('The Flickering DT', align = 'center'),
        tags$li('BAD: does re-render entire table when change valid entry'),
        tags$li('GOOD: displays validation message when numeric input <= 300'),
        br(),
        DT::dataTableOutput('flickering_dt')
      )
    )
  ),

  server = function(input, output, session) {

    # 'need'-type validation function ----
    good_to_go <- function() {
      if(input$numeric_input > 300) {        # an arbitrary requirement on 'integer'
        NULL                                 # test passed, proceed...
      } else {
        'Input gotta be greater than 300!'   # test failed, display message...
      }
    }

    # df to display in each DT ----
    my_data <- reactive({

      # first, validate input
      validate(
        good_to_go()
      )

      # if input valid, build the df
      data.frame(

        Name = c('My Integer',
                 'My Slider'),

        Value = as.character(c(input$numeric_input,
                               input$slider_input)),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    })

    # display proxy-supported NON-FLICKERING DT ----
    #  * error msg IS NOT displayed on invalid input
    #  * data wrapped in isolate()
    # details in final comment (by yihui) at https://github.com/rstudio/DT/issues/168
    output$non_flickering_dt <- DT::renderDataTable(

      rownames = FALSE,

      isolate(my_data()) # wrap data in isolate() to eliminate re-rendering the whole megillah
    )

    # proxy for non-flickering DT
    proxy = dataTableProxy('non_flickering_dt')

    observe({

      replaceData(proxy, my_data(), rownames = FALSE
      )
    })

    # display FLICKERING DT ----
    #  * error msg IS displayed on invalid input
    #  * data NOT wrapped in isolate()
    output$flickering_dt <- DT::renderDataTable(

      rownames = FALSE,

      {my_data()}        # data not wrapped in isolate()
    )
  })

I thus far have been unable to get the desired effect: no flickering — which requires wrapping the data in isolate() — and displaying an error message when invalid data are entered in an input.

I apparently do not understand the reactive model well enough to work around this issue and will appreciate any guidance.

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Just a quick note to announce the release on CRAN of the rclipboard package (https://cran.r-project.org/package=rclipboard).

This is a small package which provides a reactive copy-to-clipboard UI button component, called 'rclipButton', to use in Shiny apps. In the background, the package leverages the functionality of 'clipboard.js', a JavaScript library for HMTL5-based copy to clipboard from web pages (see <https://clipboardjs.com> for more information). So no reliance on Flash!

Note that this UI component unfortunately works only in apps deployed on a server, due to some limitations in the current RStudio web engine (see https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/1537 for more details), However, a simple workaround is illustrated in https://github.com/sbihorel/rclipboard for apps that need to be deployed for local use in RStudio in addition to remote use.

I hope this helps.

Sebastien
